title: The Maya, Aztecs and Inca

cards.h: Three huge civilisations that never knew Rome or China existed
cards.b:
While Europe, Asia and Africa traded, the Americas grew their own cities, calendars and empires. Pyramids in jungles, floating gardens, and a knotted-string accounting system.

Let us meet them.

The classic Maya (about 250-900 CE) built city-states like Tikal and Palenque in today's Mexico, Guatemala and Belize. They tracked stars, used zero in their number system, and had a full writing system of glyphs. It was largely deciphered in the late 20th century, building on work by Yuri Knorozov in the 1950s.

Their kings fought wars between cities, and played a ritual ball game.

cards.h: The Aztecs: city on a lake
cards.b: The Mexica (Aztecs) founded Tenochtitlan on an island in Lake Texcoco in 1325. With causeways and farming plots called chinampas, it may have held about 200,000 people. Spaniards said it was bigger than any city they knew.

cards.h: The Inca: no writing, no problem
cards.b:
The Inca empire, Tawantinsuyu ('four parts together'), ruled from Cusco and stretched about 4,000 km along the Andes. Under Pachacuti, from about 1438, it grew quickly.

They had no writing as we know it. They kept records with quipu, knotted strings. They built a huge road network, with relay runners, and terrace farms on steep mountainsides. Machu Picchu was built around 1450.

cards.h: Why did the Aztecs and Inca fall?
cards.b:
In 1519, Hernan Cortes landed in Mexico with a small force and many native allies who resented Aztec rule. Tenochtitlan fell in 1521. Smallpox, new to the Americas, killed huge numbers.

In 1532, Francisco Pizarro trapped the Inca ruler Atahualpa at Cajamarca. The Inca were already weakened by a civil war and by disease.

In the 800s-900s, many southern Maya cities were abandoned. Possible reasons include drought, war and over-farming. Historians still argue about the weight of each.

But the Maya themselves did not disappear. Millions of Maya people live in Mexico and Guatemala today and speak Mayan languages.

cards.h: Did the Maya predict the end of the world in 2012?
cards.b:
Myth: yes.Fact: the Maya Long Count calendar completed a major cycle, a b'ak'tun, on 21 December 2012. That was like a car odometer turning over. Maya texts mention dates thousands of years in the future. There was no doomsday prophecy.

Another myth: 'the Aztecs mistook Cortes for a god'. This idea is now seen as post-conquest legend by many historians.

Five things to remember

  1. The Maya had zero, a calendar and a glyph script.
  2. Tenochtitlan was a lake city of about 200,000.
  3. The Inca used quipu and roads without writing.
  4. Cortes fell on Tenochtitlan in 1521; Pizarro took Atahualpa in 1532.
  5. Maya people are still here.

Think about it

  • Why do big empires fall quickly when disease strikes?
  • What does zero in both India and Maya say about independent invention?
